raw: “I remember a neighbor unpacking groceries with one hand because her baby was asleep in her other arm. My attention went to the baby first, and then I noticed the heavy jars she was trying to put away. It struck me how awkward that was—having something you need to get done while you’re holding someone who needs you. I felt for her. I helped put the heavy jars away. It was a small thing, but watching her manage everything one-handed made me want to take a little of the work off her.”
